svg.text: SHARED MEMORY BANK CONFLICTS — FROM PHYSICS TO SWIZZLE
each bank serves ONE 4-byte word per cycle · warp = 32 lanes served in parallel = 128 B/cycle
word w → bank (w mod 32) · lane t reads word t → bank t → 32 banks in parallel = 1 CYCLE
bonus: lanes reading the SAME word are free too (broadcast) — conflicts need DIFFERENT words, same bank
lane t reads word 2t → bank (2t mod 32) → lanes 0–15 and 16–31 hit the SAME 16 banks
2 lanes per bank → 2-WAY CONFLICT → 2 cycles (2× slower)
stride 32 (a matrix column) would put ALL 32 lanes on ONE bank → 32-way → 32 cycles
3 · CLASSIC DISASTER: 32×32 f32 TILE, READ A COLUMN (row-major, naive)
cell color = bank it lives in · lane r reads element (r, col=5) → word r·32+5 → bank 5 EVERY time
4 · THE FIX: XOR SWIZZLE — store (r,c) at word r·32 + (c ⊕ r)
same data, permuted placement · now lane r reads bank (5 ⊕ r) → all 32 banks, distinct
column read now touches 32 distinct banks → 1 CYCLE
…and every ROW is still conflict-free too — XOR is a permutation per row
N lanes → different words, same bank
ncu Source view flags the exact SASS line

why swizzle over padding: padding wastes smem (3% for 33-pitch) and breaks TMA's fixed box layout — XOR swizzle is lossless and is exactly what TMA's 32B/64B/128B swizzle modes + ldmatrix implement in hardware
on sm_100 the swizzle ALSO feeds tcgen05's SMEM descriptors; on sm_120 it feeds ldmatrix — same conflict math either way
